_comment: Load gate for tests/load/run.py. The measurements themselves, and the hardware each
number came from, are in docs/perf.md.
max_p95_ratio is the regression gate, and it is deliberately tighter than the 1.2x the
documentation promises: GCM measures 0.80-0.95 of the CBC builtin on this workload, so a
1.2 gate has a quarter of its range in dead space and a doubling of per-row cost would
pass unnoticed. It is not tighter still because of measured noise, not caution. Six CI
runs put the worst observed ratio at 0.947, all of them at one session — the axis with
40 samples where 8 and 32 sessions have 320 and 1280, and correspondingly a 1.19x
run-to-run spread against 1.06x and 1.04x. 1.10 clears the worst observation by 16% and
sits about 26% above the centre of the distribution, so it fails on a regression rather
max_p95_ms_at_largest_serial stays at the 1s promise from docs/design.md §1.2. Observed:
235-266 ms across six runs. It is an absolute number on a shared runner whose hardware
is not ours to pin, so tightening it would buy sensitivity by trading it for failures
that say nothing about this component. The ratio is the noise-immune metric and is where
Raising either number needs a PR that states the hardware, the server version and why
the regression is acceptable, and updates docs/perf.md in the same change.
